security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation examples, not executable behavior. Hardcoded URLs, TestPyPI references, private index examples, .pypirc guidance, and markdown backticks are expected Python packaging material.

remediation.issue: Credential examples mention .pypirc and API tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning to keep .pypirc out of source control and use scoped PyPI tokens.

remediation.issue: Private index examples can change package trust boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify private package indexes and avoid replacing PyPI unless they intend to do so.

content.value_statement: Python packaging has many files, standards, and release steps. This skill gives practical patterns for building packages, CLIs, wheels, and PyPI releases.
actual_capabilities: Design source-layout and flat-layout Python package structures.
Create pyproject.toml metadata for libraries and CLI tools.
Define dependencies, optional extras, entry points, and classifiers.
Build source distributions and wheels for local verification.
Plan TestPyPI, PyPI, and private index publishing workflows.
Draft README, MANIFEST.in, .gitignore, and release checklists.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a hosted package registry.
It cannot verify package names or credentials without external checks.
It does not replace security review of dependencies or release artifacts.
Private repository setup still depends on the user's organization.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Library Release
use_cases.description: Create package metadata, build artifacts, and release checks for a reusable Python library.

use_cases.title: Ship a Python CLI
use_cases.description: Configure entry points, dependencies, and packaging structure for an installable command-line tool.

use_cases.title: Standardize Internal Packages
use_cases.description: Document project layout, private index usage, and publishing steps for organization-wide Python packages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a minimal Python package named [package-name] with pyproject.toml, README guidance, and a source layout.

prompt_templates.title: Add CLI Packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn my Python module into an installable CLI package. Include entry point metadata, dependency guidance, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for PyPI Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Python package release plan. Cover build commands, TestPyPI validation, versioning, tokens, and final PyPI publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Design Advanced Packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Design packaging for a multi-package Python project with optional extras, namespace packages, data files, and private index distribution.

output_examples.input: I need to package a small Python library for PyPI.
output: Recommended source layout with required project files.

output_examples.input: I want users to install my Python command as a terminal tool.
output: Entry point plan for the CLI command.
README sections for installation and usage.

output_examples.input: My team publishes packages to a private index.
output: Private index configuration points to verify.
Token handling and access control reminders.

best_practices: Use pyproject.toml as the primary packaging configuration.
Build and test artifacts in an isolated environment before publishing.
Use scoped API tokens and keep publishing credentials out of source control.
anti_patterns: Publishing directly to PyPI before testing the package artifact.
Pinning every dependency exactly without a clear compatibility reason.
Embedding private credentials or repository tokens in project files.

faq.question: Does this skill create package files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structure, examples, and checklists that an AI coding agent can apply to your project.

faq.question: Can it help with pyproject.toml?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers project metadata, build backends, dependencies, optional extras, scripts, and classifiers.

faq.question: Does it support CLI tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for console entry points and common CLI packaging patterns.

faq.question: Can it publish to PyPI for me?
faq.answer: It can guide the release workflow, but publishing still requires user approval, credentials, and final verification.

faq.question: Does it cover private package indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes private index examples and should be used with trusted repository settings.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing packages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help modernize package structure, metadata, build steps, and release documentation.
